title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 131
paragraphs: That is how matters stood with the judgment of the suitors, and how the Alcmaeonidae became famous throughout Greece. From this marriage was born that Cleisthenes who established the tribes and the democracy for the Athenians — named after his maternal grandfather, the Sicyonian Cleisthenes. He was the son of Megacles; Megacles also had another son, Hippocrates, from whom came another Megacles and another Agariste, named after the Agariste who was daughter of Cleisthenes. This Agariste married Xanthippus son of Ariphron, and when she was pregnant she saw a dream in which it seemed to her that she had given birth to a lion. A few days later she bore to Xanthippus a son: Pericles.
